question: Is the ~81.6 mA powered-host backfeed a wirepad (USB) path, and does the island_support reverse-blocking switch remove it?

finding.path: Host-interface outputs on provider gf180mcu_fd_io__bi_t cells (D2H_CLK, D2H_D[0..9], HOST_MISO: 12 sites) with the chip unpowered and the host powered: current flows from the host through each provider pad's upper ESD/drain junction into the common DVDD ring and out through the off board supply.
finding.not_wirepad: The wirepad (USB/TMDS) pads do not carry this path: with a 3.63 V/50 ohm peer and the chip off they draw 0.87 mA/leg (tt) to 6.7 mA/leg (ff/85C) into the isolated protection rail and shunt, with <=10 nA into the supply (family-sims.json). The earlier report wrongly listed the 81.6 mA under wirepad.
finding.island_switch: No effect: the island_support body-switched PMOS blocks island-rail -> ring current (<=0.33 uA), but this current enters the ring itself through the provider pad junctions, upstream of every island switch.

damage_risk.per_pin: ~6.8 mA DC per provider pad junction; the provider diode area is far above the DRM 14.2 contact/via EM limits at this current, so no EM or thermal damage is expected for bench durations
damage_risk.ring: The ring is held near 0 V only because the off board supply sinks 81.6 mA. If the board supply is disconnected (floating) the host phantom-powers the ring toward ~2.6 V through the junctions: undefined partial power-up, POR uncertainty and forward-biased I/O junctions (DRM 14.3 I/O latch-up rules apply to such junctions).
damage_risk.host: The FPGA sources ~6.8 mA per pin into a low impedance; within typical FPGA drive limits but continuous.

proposal.on_chip: Not available with the provider bi_t cell: the junction to DVDD is intrinsic to the provider cell. A custom isolated-rail pad for 12 x 312.5 MHz host lines would need a full redesign and area; not proposed for this die.
board_requirement: Host I/Os toward the chip must be high-impedance (no keepers/pull-ups, outputs tristated) whenever the chip supply is below 3.15 V; FPGA configuration holds them high-Z until the chip POR/power-good is observed.

Preferred hardware enforcement: a FET bus switch with Ioff/powered-off isolation and >=500 MHz bandwidth (e.g. a TS3L/SN74CB3Q-class part) on the 12 host lines, enabled from the chip-side 3.3 V rail; external parts allowed.
Series resistors are not suitable on the 312.5 MHz D2H lines (1 kohm would limit the backfeed to ~2.7 mA/pin but destroys the edge rate); acceptable only on HOST_MISO/SPI-rate lines.
Never leave the chip supply floating while the host is powered: the board supply must present a defined (off = grounded) state or the bus switch must be open.

wirepad_safe: pass for its own pads (pulses, ramps, powered peer); the host-interface backfeed belongs to the host/digital pad block and the supply ring
